full_judgment:
S.M. Husain, J: This Civil Revision Case is directed against a concurrent judgment of affirmance of the courts below decreeing a suit challenging the dismissal of the plaintiff by the management of Sonali Bank. 

 5. Thus it would clearly appear that the judgment of the courts below decreeing the plaintiff's suit clearly suffer from illegality. In this connection it may be observed that the plaintiff filed a suit only for a declaration that the plaintiff's dismissal by the Bank was illegal and not binding upon him and that he was still in service. This prayer for declaration was not followed by any consequential relief by way of any mandatory injunction and direction against the Bank to allow the plaintiff to continue in the service of the Bank and also by way of any claim for arrear wages and compensation and damages. Omission to pray for any consequential relief for the purpose of enforcing a declaratory decree would be hit by the provision to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Upon such ground the declaratory decree passed by the courts below becomes unenforceable; which in turn would make the decree a nullity. 

 6. Be that as it may, the judgment and decree of both the courts below suffer from patent illegality and are thus set aside. The plaintiff's suit for declaration that his dismissal from service under the defendant was illegal stands dismissed. This Rule is made absolute. There will be no order as to costs.
